summary.text: Simcha Felder represents the 44th District on the New York City Council, which includes Borough Park, Flatbush, Gravesend, Mapleton and Midwood in Brooklyn.
His Council biography says he was first elected to the Council in 2002 and also served in the State Senate before returning to the Council.

paragraphs.text: Felder is a lifelong Brooklynite who grew up, married and raised four children in the same neighborhood, according to his Council biography.
He is a Certified Public Accountant with an MBA in management from Baruch College's Zicklin School of Business and has taught management at Touro University and Brooklyn College.

Outside elected office he was Deputy Comptroller for Budget, Accounting, Administration and IT in the New York City Comptroller's Office, and held roles in the State Assembly and the Department of Finance.

On the Council he sponsored the five-minute grace period for parking violations, and the biography says he turned empty city-owned lots into housing, playgrounds and a Hatzolah Volunteer Ambulance garage.
It says that in the State Senate he secured funding for door-to-door school transportation and passed legislation on resources for parents of special education students.
